blocks.html:
READING PASSAGE 2

You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 14-26, which are based on Reading Passage 2 on the following pages.

Born to Trade

Long before our ancestors had any trappings of civilisation, they had a taste for material goods. Kate Douglas discovers where this ancient obsession has led us.

Section A (Q14):

A Humans are born to trade and we don't need shops or money to do it—the heart of commerce is an instinctive ability for what anthropologists call “reciprocity”. This is an ability to exchange goods of equal worth, and it evolved as the brains of our ancient ancestors and societies became more complex, allowing individuals to keep a running tally of their interactions with others. Evidence from modern hunter-gatherers leaves little doubt that the exchange of food and favours is innate, as is the ability to keep track of the credits and debits that accrue as a result. Combine this skill for mental book-keeping with even the most basic material culture, and trade inevitably follows.

Section B (Q15):

B Once trade gets off the ground, the economic benefits quickly make it irresistible. But exchanging tools, food and other essentials of life in a barter economy is a far cry from the shopping mall. Modern consumerism extends beyond subsistence and utilitarianism to encompass everything from Gucci handbags and BMW convertibles to valuable paintings. Clearly, the worth of such goods is not inherent but resides in certain intangible qualities that we invest in them. When did humans start holding these goods in such high esteem?

Section C (Q16):

C All the archaeological evidence for the flowering of consumer culture has up to now pointed to a date of around 40,000 years ago. That's when early modern humans started making increasingly intricate bone and stone tools, carving patterns into rocks and creating representational art such as carved figurines, jewellery and cave paintings. However, discoveries in Africa are pushing the origins of consumerism much further back into human prehistory.

A few years ago, reports began to emerge of discoveries made at the Blombos Cave, a site of ancient human habitation in South Africa. Christopher Henshilwood and colleagues from the University of Bergen in Norway dated thousands of pieces of ochre from the cave, and many of them proved to be more than 100,000 years old — before the time that early humans moved out of Africa. Ochre, a coloured clay that comes in various shades from red to black, does not occur naturally around Blombos and must have been imported from quarries at least 30 kilometres away, either directly by Blombos residents or through trade. Although ochre can be used to dry and preserve (cure) animal hides, the researchers are convinced the Blombos ochre had a symbolic purpose. For a start, it is predominantly red—any of the other colours available would have done for curing—and the surfaces of the clay had been scraped in a way that indicates they were used to yield pigment for dyes.

Section D (Q17):

D An even more intriguing discovery from Blombos was of 41 beads dating from 76,000 years ago, found in clusters and made from the shells of a tiny mollusc. These cannot be natural deposits, argue the researchers, as each cluster contains shells of a similar size and colour with consistently placed holes. What's more, all the beads display a pattern of wear suggesting friction from rubbing against thread, clothes or other beads.

The previous oldest find of beads in Africa dates back to just 45,000 years ago. And it seems the Blombos people's taste for beautiful items was not an isolated phenomenon. Jessica Thompson of Arizona State University in Tempe has described finding shell fragments from a site in Tanzania that she believes may represent debris from bead manufacture. They are at least 45,000—and possibly 280,000—years old. Although there is no evidence of how the ancient beads were used, their modern counterparts are often traded. So it looks as though our taste for jewellery and art is much older than we thought.

Section E (Q18):

E But why did we come to value these objects in the first place? In many animal species, individuals signal their genetic fitness by showing off with attention-grabbing adornment. Some researchers think that in humans, consumer products play a similar role. Archaeologist Aimee Plourde, from the University of California, also argues that even in egalitarian societies, some people are more successful than others. Among our ancestors, superior skills in areas such as hunting, crafts, environmental knowledge and contact with neighbouring groups would have brought respect—in other words, prestige.

And because prestige brings social benefits, people would want to show off their talents. The best way to do this would be through demonstrating possession of material items that are hard to fake. ‘A good hunter, for instance, could advertise his skills by wearing the tooth of an animal that is elusive or dangerous,' says Plourde. The benefits of prestige would also lead to competition to acquire it. As a result, the value and variety of prestige goods would spiral and there would be a parallel increase in the ranking of social systems.

If Plourde is correct, prestige goods form a direct link between our innate drive for trade and the development of structured, hierarchical societies. They are arguably the first step on the road to modern civilisation, paving the way for agriculture and urbanisation. We may not be impressed by beads any more, but their modern equivalents have the same fascination. Nobody believes the guy who spends €670,000 on a Bugatti Veyron car does so because he needs to travel at 250 mph. We all know in today's consumer society he's buying an exclusive status symbol.

Questions 14–18

Reading Passage 2 has five sections, A–E.

Choose the correct heading for each section from the list of headings below.

Write the correct number, i–vii, in boxes 14–18 on your answer sheet. (Drag a heading from this list and drop it onto the correct section's answer box on the left.)

List of Headings
i The desire to make expensive jewellery
ii The clues that indicate ancient items were decorative
iii Querying the changes in the value of traded items
iv A natural human talent
v How status can be gained from ownership of goods
vi Recent finds alter theories about when consumerism started
vii Changes in research methods

Questions 19–21

Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

Write the correct letter in boxes 19–21 on your answer sheet.

21 What made the researchers realise the purpose of the beads found at Blombos Cave?

Questions 22–26

Complete the summary below.

Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.

Why certain objects are valued?

Some researchers argue that we may use ownership of desirable goods to demonstrate our strength and fitness as other 22 use their attractive physical features. Showing off one's superiority is not a new phenomenon and even in ancient times successful people would have gained 23 from this. A desire for status could have led to an increase in the worth of prestige goods and to 24 among people wishing to achieve this status.

It is thought that our natural desire to trade provided a basis for organised farming and 25 development and finally resulted in the complex societies which can be seen today. Whilst we do not value things such as beads nowadays, other items hold the same appeal for us and bring the same status as owning beads did for our 26 .

B exploration
C trade
D settlements
E stability

meta.title: Born to Trade 交易的本能

passageNotes.label: Paragraph A
passageNotes.text: 人类天生就会交易，我们不需要商店或金钱来做到这一点——商业的核心是一种人类学家称为“互惠”的本能能力。这是一种交换等价物品的能力，随着我们远古祖先的大脑和社会变得更加复杂，这种能力逐渐进化，使个人能够持续记录自己与他人的互动。来自现代狩猎采集者的证据几乎毫无疑问地表明，食物和恩惠的交换是天生的，追踪由此产生的债权和债务的能力也是如此。将这种心理记账的技能与哪怕最基本的物质文化结合起来，交易就不可避免地随之而来。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph B
passageNotes.text: 一旦交易开始运转，其经济收益很快就变得不可抗拒。但在以物易物的经济中交换工具、食物和其他生活必需品，与购物中心相去甚远。现代消费主义超越了生存和实用主义的范畴，涵盖了从Gucci手袋和BMW敞篷车到珍贵画作的一切。显然，这些商品的价值并非固有的，而是存在于我们赋予它们的某些无形品质之中。人类是从何时开始如此高度珍视这些商品的呢？

passageNotes.label: Paragraph C
passageNotes.text:
迄今为止，所有关于消费文化兴盛的考古证据都指向大约4万年前的时期。那时，早期现代人类开始制造日益复杂的骨器和石器，在岩石上雕刻图案，并创作具象艺术，如雕刻小雕像、珠宝和洞穴壁画。然而，非洲的发现正在将消费主义的起源推回到更久远的人类史前时期。

几年前，关于南非一处古代人类居住遗址——布洛姆波斯洞穴（Blombos Cave）发现的报告开始出现。挪威卑尔根大学的Christopher Henshilwood及其同事对洞穴中数千块赭石进行了年代测定，其中许多被证明已有超过10万年的历史——早于早期人类走出非洲的时期。赭石是一种从红色到黑色不等的各种色调的彩色粘土，在布洛姆波斯周围并不自然出现，一定是从至少30公里外的采石场进口的，要么是由布洛姆波斯居民直接搬运，要么通过贸易获得。虽然赭石可以用来干燥和保存（鞣制）兽皮，但研究人员确信布洛姆波斯的赭石具有象征性的用途。首先，它主要是红色的——其他任何可用的颜色都能用于鞣制——而且粘土的表面被刮擦的方式表明，它们曾被用来提取染料用的颜料。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph D
passageNotes.text:
布洛姆波斯一个更引人入胜的发现是41颗可追溯到7.6万年前的珠子，它们成群出现，由一种微小软体动物的贝壳制成。研究人员认为，这些不可能是自然沉积物，因为每组珠子都包含大小和颜色相似、孔洞位置一致的贝壳。更重要的是，所有珠子都显示出一种磨损模式，表明它们曾与线、衣服或其他珠子发生摩擦。

此前非洲发现的最古老珠子仅可追溯到4.5万年前。而且布洛姆波斯人对美丽物品的喜爱似乎并非孤立现象。亚利桑那州立大学坦佩分校的Jessica Thompson描述了在坦桑尼亚一处遗址发现的贝壳碎片，她认为这些可能是珠子制造的残余物。它们至少有4.5万年——甚至可能28万年——的历史。虽然没有证据表明这些古代珠子是如何使用的，但它们的现代对应物常常被用于交易。因此，看起来我们对珠宝和艺术的喜爱比我们想象的要古老得多。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph E
passageNotes.text:
但我们最初为什么会珍视这些物品呢？在许多动物物种中，个体通过引人注目的装饰炫耀来展示自己的基因适应性。一些研究者认为，在人类中，消费品也扮演着类似的角色。来自加利福尼亚大学的考古学家Aimee Plourde还认为，即使在平等主义社会中，有些人也比其他人更成功。在我们的祖先中，狩猎、工艺、环境知识和与邻近群体接触等方面的卓越技能会带来尊重——换句话说，就是声望。

由于声望带来社会利益，人们会想要炫耀自己的才能。做到这一点的最佳方式是展示难以伪造的物质物品。Plourde说：“例如，一个优秀的猎人可以通过佩戴一种难以捕捉或危险的动物的牙齿来展示自己的技能。”声望的好处还会引发争夺声望的竞争。结果，声望商品的价值和种类会不断攀升，社会系统的等级划分也会随之增加。

如果Plourde是正确的，声望商品就在我们天生的交易驱动力与有组织的等级社会的发展之间建立了直接的联系。它们可以说是在通往现代文明之路上迈出的第一步，为农业和城市化铺平了道路。我们可能不再为珠子所打动，但它们的现代等价物具有同样的吸引力。没有人相信那个花67万欧元买一辆布加迪威龙（Bugatti Veyron）汽车的人这样做是因为他需要以每小时250英里的速度行驶。我们都知道，在当今的消费社会中，他购买的是一个专属的身份象征。

items.text:
（1）题目 14：（题干见题目区）
答案：iv（A natural human talent）
定位：A 部分，首句及末句
原文：Humans are born to trade and we don’t need shops or money to do it—the heart of commerce is an instinctive ability for what anthropologists call “reciprocity”.
译文：人类天生就会交易；商业的核心是一种人类本能，即人类学家所说的“互惠”。

解析：本段通篇解释互惠、心理记账与交换是人类与生俱来的能力，因此标题应为“A natural human talent”。

（2）题目 15：（题干见题目区）
答案：iii（Querying the changes in the value of traded items）
定位：B 部分，末2句
原文：Clearly, the worth of such goods is not inherent but resides in certain intangible qualities that we invest in them. When did humans start holding these goods in such high esteem?
译文：这些商品的价值并非固有，而是来自我们赋予它们的无形品质。人类从何时起开始如此看重这些商品？

解析：本段从实用交换转向现代消费，并追问商品的无形价值何时形成，对应“Querying the changes in the value of traded items”。

（3）题目 16：（题干见题目区）
答案：vi（Recent finds alter theories about when consumerism started）
定位：C 部分，第1段末2句
原文：That’s when early modern humans started making increasingly intricate bone and stone tools, carving patterns into rocks and creating representational art such as carved figurines, jewellery and cave paintings. However, discoveries in Africa are pushing the origins of consumerism much further back into human prehistory.
译文：早期现代人当时开始制作更复杂的骨器、石器和具象艺术；然而非洲的新发现把消费主义的起源进一步推向史前。

解析：旧时间线被非洲的新发现推翻，正对应“Recent finds alter theories about when consumerism started”。

（4）题目 17：（题干见题目区）
答案：ii（The clues that indicate ancient items were decorative）
定位：D 部分，第1段
原文：These cannot be natural deposits, argue the researchers, as each cluster contains shells of a similar size and colour with consistently placed holes. What’s more, all the beads display a pattern of wear suggesting friction from rubbing against thread, clothes or other beads.
译文：研究者认为这些不可能是自然沉积，因为贝壳大小和颜色相近、孔洞位置一致，而且都有与线、衣物或其他珠子摩擦造成的磨损。

解析：孔洞位置和磨损痕迹说明这些物件经过加工并作为装饰佩戴，对应“古代物件具有装饰用途的线索”。

（5）题目 18：（题干见题目区）
答案：v（How status can be gained from ownership of goods）
定位：E 部分，第1段末句及第2段
原文：Among our ancestors, superior skills in areas such as hunting, crafts, environmental knowledge and contact with neighbouring groups would have brought respect—in other words, prestige.
译文：祖先在狩猎、手工艺、环境知识和邻群交往方面的卓越技能会带来尊重，也就是声望。

解析：本部分解释人们借难以伪造的物品展示技能并获得声望，因此标题是“How status can be gained from ownership of goods”。

（1）题目 19：In section A, ‘reciprocity’ refers to our ancestors’ ability to
题目翻译：在 A 部分，“reciprocity”指祖先具有什么能力？
答案：B（monitor the balance between goods given and received）
定位：A 部分，第2句
原文：This is an ability to exchange goods of equal worth, and it evolved as the brains of our ancient ancestors and societies became more complex, allowing individuals to keep a running tally of their interactions with others.
译文：这是一种交换等值物品的能力；随着祖先大脑和社会日益复杂，它使个人能够持续记录与他人的互动往来。

解析：keep a running tally 以及 credits and debits 表示监控付出与获得的平衡，因此选“monitor the balance between goods given and received”。

（2）题目 20：What is said about the ochre found at Blombos Cave?
题目翻译：关于布隆博斯洞穴发现的赭石，文中说了什么？
答案：D（It appears it was selected for its colour.）
定位：C 部分，第2段末句
原文：For a start, it is predominantly red—any of the other colours available would have done for curing—and the surfaces of the clay had been scraped in a way that indicates they were used to yield pigment for dyes.
译文：首先，这些赭石主要是红色；用于鞣制时其他颜色也可以，而其表面刮痕表明它们被用来获取染料颜料。

解析：其他颜色同样可用于鞣制却主要选择红色，说明选择标准是颜色，因此选 D。

（3）题目 21：What made the researchers realise the purpose of the beads found at Blombos Cave?
题目翻译：研究者根据什么判断布隆博斯洞穴珠子的用途？
答案：D（They have holes and markings suggesting they were joined together.）
定位：D 部分，第1段末2句
原文：each cluster contains shells of a similar size and colour with consistently placed holes. What’s more, all the beads display a pattern of wear suggesting friction from rubbing against thread, clothes or other beads.

解析：位置一致的孔洞加上摩擦磨损共同表明珠子曾被串联或佩戴，因此选 D。

解析：位置一致的孔洞加上摩擦磨损共同表明珠子曾被串联或佩戴，因此选 D。

items.text:
（1）题目 22：Some researchers argue that we may use ownership of desirable goods to demonstrate our strength and fitness as other ________ use their attractive physical features. Showing off one’s superiority is not a new phenomenon and even in ancient times successful people would have gained ________ from this. A desire for status could have led to an increase in the worth of prestige goods and to ________ among people wishing to achieve this status.
题目翻译：一些研究者认为，人类借贵重物品展示强壮和适应力，就像其他________借醒目的身体特征进行展示。
答案：I（species）
定位：E 部分，第1段第2句
原文：In many animal species, individuals signal their genetic fitness by showing off with attention-grabbing adornment.
译文：在许多动物物种中，个体会通过醒目的装饰展示其遗传适应力。

解析：other 后需要复数类属名词；原文的 animal species 直接对应选项 species。

（2）题目 23：Some researchers argue that we may use ownership of desirable goods to demonstrate our strength and fitness as other ________ use their attractive physical features. Showing off one’s superiority is not a new phenomenon and even in ancient times successful people would have gained ________ from this. A desire for status could have led to an increase in the worth of prestige goods and to ________ among people wishing to achieve this status.
题目翻译：即使在古代，成功者也会由此获得________。
答案：F（respect）
定位：E 部分，第1段末句
原文：Among our ancestors, superior skills in areas such as hunting, crafts, environmental knowledge and contact with neighbouring groups would have brought respect—in other words, prestige.
译文：祖先的卓越技能会带来尊重，换言之即声望。

解析：gained 与原文 brought 对应，空格应填 respect。

（3）题目 24：Some researchers argue that we may use ownership of desirable goods to demonstrate our strength and fitness as other ________ use their attractive physical features. Showing off one’s superiority is not a new phenomenon and even in ancient times successful people would have gained ________ from this. A desire for status could have led to an increase in the worth of prestige goods and to ________ among people wishing to achieve this status.
题目翻译：对地位的渴望可能使声望物品升值，也导致追求这一地位的人之间出现________。
答案：A（competitiveness）
定位：E 部分，第2段第4句
原文：The benefits of prestige would also lead to competition to acquire it.
译文：声望带来的好处也会导致人们为获得声望而竞争。

解析：competition 在题干中变为介词 to 后的名词 competitiveness，语义与语法均吻合。

（4）题目 25：It is thought that our natural desire to trade provided a basis for organised farming and ________ development and finally resulted in the complex societies which can be seen today. Whilst we do not value things such as beads nowadays, other items hold the same appeal for us and bring the same status as owning beads did for our ________.
题目翻译：人类天生的交易欲望为农业和________发展奠定基础。
答案：J（city）
定位：E 部分，第3段第2句
原文：They are arguably the first step on the road to modern civilisation, paving the way for agriculture and urbanisation.
译文：它们可说是通往现代文明的第一步，为农业和城市化铺平道路。

解析：urbanisation 在摘要中改写为 city development，因此选 city。

（5）题目 26：It is thought that our natural desire to trade provided a basis for organised farming and ________ development and finally resulted in the complex societies which can be seen today. Whilst we do not value things such as beads nowadays, other items hold the same appeal for us and bring the same status as owning beads did for our ________.
题目翻译：现代物品带来的地位，与珠子曾带给我们________的地位相同。
答案：H（ancestors）
定位：E 部分，第1段末句
原文：Among our ancestors, superior skills in areas such as hunting, crafts, environmental knowledge and contact with neighbouring groups would have brought respect—in other words, prestige.
译文：在我们的祖先中，卓越技能会带来尊重，也就是声望。

解析：摘要把古代佩戴珠子的人概括为 our ancestors，因此选 ancestors。
